cards.front: What is [[kw:depreciation]]?
back: The systematic allocation of an asset's cost over its useful life.
It does **not** measure decline in market value.
Matches expense to revenue generated.

cards.front: Define [[kw:depreciable cost]].
back: $$\text{Depreciable Cost} = \text{Asset Cost} - \text{Residual Value}$$
This is the total amount to be depreciated over the asset's life.
Residual value is the estimated salvage or trade‑in value at the end.
$$\text{Book Value} = \text{Asset Cost} - \text{Accumulated Depreciation}$$
It cannot be less than residual value.
It represents the undepreciated portion of the asset.
cards.front: What is [[kw:book value]]?
What is the [[kw:straight‑line depreciation]] formula?
back: $$\text{Annual Depreciation} = \frac{\text{Cost} - \text{Residual Value}}{\text{Useful Life}}$$
Allocates equal expense each year.
Most commonly used method.
Depreciable cost = $12,000.
Annual depreciation = $12,000 ÷ 6 = $2,000.
cards.front: Calculate straight‑line: cost $15,000, residual $3,000, life 6 years.

back: A table showing each year's depreciation expense, accumulated depreciation, and book value.
Under straight‑line, expense is constant; accumulated grows; book value declines.
Final book value equals residual value.
cards.front: What is a [[kw:depreciation schedule]]?
How do you calculate [[kw:partial‑year depreciation]]?
back: $$\text{Partial Depreciation} = \text{Annual Depreciation} \times \frac{\text{Months in Service}}{12}$$
Used when an asset is purchased partway through the fiscal year.
The remaining depreciation extends into a later year.
Months used: Aug–Dec = 5 months.
The remaining $1,400 is taken in the year after normal life ends.
cards.front: Annual depreciation $2,400, asset bought on August 1. First‑year depreciation?

back: Depreciation based on actual usage (miles, hours, units).
$$\text{Depreciation per Unit} = \frac{\text{Cost} - \text{Residual}}{\text{Total Estimated Units}}$$
Annual expense varies with usage.
cards.front: What is the [[kw:units‑of‑production method]]?
A truck costs $30,000, residual $5,000, estimated 200,000 miles. Find rate per mile.

back: $$\text{Annual Depreciation} = \text{Depreciation per Unit} \times \text{Actual Units Used}$$
Example: rate $0.125/mile, driven 40,000 miles → $5,000 expense.
cards.front: How is units‑of‑production annual depreciation computed?
What happens if actual units exceed total estimated units?
back: Depreciation stops once accumulated depreciation equals depreciable cost.
No further expense is recorded even if the asset is still used.
Book value remains at residual value.

cards.front: Compare total depreciation under straight‑line and units‑of‑production.
back: Total depreciation over life is the same = Cost – Residual.
Only the timing differs.
Straight‑line is time‑based; units‑of‑production is usage‑based.
An accelerated method recording more depreciation in early years.
Applies a constant rate to the declining book value.
Common version: double‑declining‑balance (DDB).
cards.front: What is the [[kw:declining‑balance method]]?

back: $$\text{DDB Rate} = \frac{2}{\text{Useful Life}}$$
Example: 5‑year life → DDB rate = 2/5 = 40%.
Residual value is NOT subtracted when calculating the rate.
cards.front: How is the [[kw:double‑declining‑balance (DDB) rate]] calculated?
How is annual DDB depreciation computed?
back: $$\text{Annual Depreciation} = \text{Beginning Book Value} \times \text{DDB Rate}$$
Expense decreases each year because book value shrinks.
Never depreciate below residual value.

cards.front: A machine costs $20,000, 5‑year life, DDB rate 40%. Year 1 depreciation?

back: Do NOT subtract residual before multiplying by the rate.
But if the calculated expense would push book value below residual, cap the expense.
Cap = Book Value – Residual.
cards.front: What is the rule for residual value under DDB?
When do companies switch from DDB to straight‑line?
back: When straight‑line on the remaining book value gives a higher depreciation than DDB.
Compute SL = (Book Value – Residual) / Remaining Life.
If SL ≥ DDB, switch permanently.
All three methods depreciate the same total amount: Cost – Residual.
Only the annual pattern differs.
DDB is accelerated; straight‑line is constant; units‑of‑production varies.
cards.front: Compare total depreciation among straight‑line, units‑of‑production, and DDB.

back: [[imp:Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System – the IRS‑required tax depreciation method.]]
Depreciates assets to zero over prescribed recovery periods.
Uses a half‑year convention.
cards.front: What is [[kw:MACRS]]?

back: MACRS is for tax returns; GAAP is for financial statements.
MACRS ignores residual value; GAAP considers it.
MACRS uses IRS‑specified recovery periods and rates.
cards.front: How is MACRS different from GAAP depreciation?

back: Assumes assets are placed in service at mid‑year.
Year 1 gets half the full‑year depreciation; the other half is taken in an extra year.
A 5‑year property depreciates over 6 tax years.
cards.front: What is the [[kw:half‑year convention]]?

back: Year 1: 20%
Year 2: 32%
Apply these rates to the original cost each year.
cards.front: Give the MACRS rates for 5‑year property (years 1‑3).

back: Year 1 rate = 20%.
cards.front: Calculate Year 1 MACRS depreciation for a $10,000 computer (5‑year).
What is the MACRS recovery period for office furniture?
back: 7 years.
Computers: 5 years. Residential rental property: 27.5 years.
Recovery periods are set by the IRS, not by the company.
To simplify and accelerate deductions.
Assets are depreciated to zero regardless of expected salvage.
This maximizes tax deductions over the recovery period.
cards.front: Why does MACRS ignore residual value?
How do you build a [[kw:MACRS depreciation schedule]]?
back: 1. Identify the asset's recovery class.
2. Multiply original cost by the year's table rate.
3. Accumulated depreciation = sum; adjusted basis = cost – accumulated.
Rates sum to 100%; asset is fully depreciated.
[[imp:Understand:]] cost, residual, useful life, purchase date.
[[imp:Solve:]] compute depreciable cost, annual depreciation, build schedule if needed.
[[imp:Conclude:]] verify final book value equals residual.
cards.front: What is the blueprint for straight‑line depreciation problems?

back: [[imp:Understand:]] cost, recovery class, tax year.
[[imp:Solve:]] use the IRS table rate; multiply cost by rate.
[[imp:Conclude:]] verify rates sum to 100%.
